artwork: Twenty original Hearth20 colored 3D sculptures. Creature subjects are from the fifth-edition Monster Manual; these are original depictions, not extracted official art or third-party models.

creatures.name: Adult Red Dragon
creatures.tagline: A crown of horn and flame
tips: Red dragons are chromatic dragons, feared for fire and territorial pride.
A dragon encounter can unfold above the party as well as around it.
Spread the party before a cone of dragon breath catches everyone together.
The oldest treasure in a hoard may matter more than its gold value.
Drag the model to inspect its wings, horns and armored belly.
Right-drag up or down to lift the model slightly in the viewer.
Choose Fire in FX for turbulent flame; changing its tint keeps the fire material.
Breath is a cast effect: drag from the dragon toward its target.
Use a 60-degree measuring cone to plan a dragon's threat area.
Cosmetic fire never spends resources or applies damage; the DM resolves the outcome.

creatures.name: Beholder
tips: A beholder's central eye and smaller eyestalks serve different purposes.
Its central gaze is associated with antimagic, while the stalks project magical rays.
A floating enemy makes cover and room height worth describing aloud.
Suspicion is a useful theme for a lair built by a many-eyed tyrant.
Rotate this model to see the separate stalks instead of a flat creature image.
Magic material draws arcane knotwork; Holy material forms crisp glints and facets.
A beam has a trajectory, so drag its source and release at the target.
The DM can hide a creature token until the party discovers it.
Opening a player-view preview shows the host-filtered view for that player.
Use the model and tip controls freely; a fast load does not force a waiting period.

creatures.name: Mind Flayer
tips: The mind flayer combines an alien, tentacled appearance with formidable psychic power.
Telepathy can make an encounter unsettling without a single spoken word.
A psychic threat may demand a different plan from an armored brute.
Prisoners, thralls and strange machinery can tell a lair's story before combat starts.
Drag horizontally to examine the model's four facial tentacles and high collar.
Magic FX use moving glyph rings rather than a recolored fireball.
Use an instant burst for a psychic impact at the cursor, without a cast line.
Choose Only me when a roll should stay out of the public table history.
A player's display name is separate from their saved signing identity.
Someone using the same display name does not inherit another player's token grants.

creatures.name: Owlbear
tips: An owlbear combines a bear's heavy frame with an owl-like head and beak.
Its silhouette is a warning even before anyone recognizes the creature.
Tracks, torn trees and an abandoned nest can introduce the danger gradually.
A protective parent can create a tense encounter without an evil villain.
The viewer's scroll wheel moves the camera closer or farther away.
Tokens are controlled by the DM until the DM explicitly grants a player access.
The Tokens side button places a new creature where you click and release.
New creature tokens begin concealed; reveal them when the party can discover them.
Use Blood for wet splashes and mist instead of red sparks.
Adjust grid opacity on a busy forest map so movement remains easy to read.

creatures.name: Mimic
tips: A mimic's disguise turns an ordinary object into an unexpected creature.
Its adhesive nature makes careless touching particularly dangerous.
A chest is a familiar disguise, but furniture can be suspicious too.
Leave clues that reward a cautious player before springing an ambush.
This model has an opening lid-jaw, individual teeth and a sculpted tongue.
Give the token an innocent name until you choose to reveal its identity.
The DM layer can hold a secret token before it enters the public token layer.
An impact appears where the left mouse button is released; it needs no trajectory.
The Slime material stretches into sticky strands and bubbling surfaces.
Save the campaign after changing control grants so they survive the next session.

creatures.name: Gelatinous Cube
tips: A gelatinous cube is a nearly transparent ooze shaped by the passages it travels.
Objects suspended inside an ooze can be a clue rather than free treasure.
An unnaturally clean dungeon corridor deserves a closer look.
Describe what the characters notice before demanding a tactical decision.
Rotate the colored translucent model to find the bones and coins inside.
Water and Slime are separate FX materials with different movement and surfaces.
Pooling and bubbling effects stay at the release point on the board.
Grid thickness is measured in screen pixels so lines stay readable as you zoom.
A player sees authorized map pixels, not the DM's complete original image.
Blackout clears the player's board while preserving their own sheet.

creatures.name: Goblin
tips: Goblins favor mobility, opportunistic attacks and a quick escape.
A small creature can turn narrow passages into a tactical advantage.
Scouting, alarms and retreat routes make a goblin camp feel organized.
A frightened lookout can matter as much as the strongest warrior.
The loading viewer supports arrow keys as well as mouse dragging.
Use K to open Tokens and control grants while preparing an encounter.
A saved player can be assigned a token even while they are offline.
Granting one token does not grant control of every creature on the board.
Use beacons to show the party a destination without revealing hidden artwork.
A player's remembered display name makes the returning group easier to identify.

creatures.name: Orc
tips: The 2014 orc stat block emphasizes closing the distance with an enemy.
An orc warband can have scouts, rivalries and goals beyond its next fight.
Terrain can turn a straightforward advance into a difficult decision.
Not every encounter with an armed group needs to end in combat.
The model's armor and skin have separate colored materials.
Use Tokens to rename, resize, reveal and assign a selected creature.
Exploration movement can be allowed without giving the player DM editing tools.
The DM can revoke control by setting Controlled by to DM only.
Choose a thicker, brighter grid over dark dungeon floor textures.
The measuring beam offers widths of five, ten and fifteen feet.

creatures.name: Kobold
creatures.tagline: A small foe with a larger scheme
tips: Kobolds are small reptilian humanoids with a strong association with dragons.
Coordinated opponents can be more dangerous than their individual strength suggests.
Traps, tight tunnels and warning systems suit a carefully planned kobold lair.
A retreat can lure pursuers toward terrain the defenders know well.
Inspect the model's horns, tail and spear by rotating it around the vertical axis.
Grid squares and token size are separate: a small token still moves on the same grid.
Use the ruler's waypoints to measure a route around obstacles.
Closed doors stop sight and light until the DM opens them.
Rotate board north to change the direction of natural light through windows.
Use Escape to cancel token placement before you release it onto the map.

creatures.name: Troll
creatures.tagline: A wound that will not stay open
tips: A troll is famous for regeneration and a relentless appetite.
Fire and acid are important considerations when facing a regenerating troll.
Show a wound knitting together so players can discover the danger in play.
A bridge, cavern or flooded passage can make a troll encounter memorable.
The sculpture's long arms and hooked nose distinguish it from the stockier ogre.
Acid FX bubble, spray and vaporize; Fire uses turbulent flame and smoke.
Changing an FX color preserves the chosen material's appearance and motion.
A cosmetic acid splash does not automatically disable regeneration.
The DM remains responsible for recording conditions, damage and other outcomes.
Preview an effect locally before showing it to the rest of the table.

creatures.name: Ogre
creatures.tagline: Heavy steps in a narrow hall
tips: An ogre's great size and strength make it a dangerous close-range threat.
A brute with a simple goal can still change the shape of an encounter.
Broken doors and oversized footprints can reveal an ogre before it appears.
A narrow route may force a large creature to approach differently.
This sculpture uses a broad belly, heavy club and distinct giant proportions.
Set a Large token to two grid squares when that suits the encounter's scale.
Token placement starts at the cursor; the DM can move the piece freely afterward.
A token's controller is explicit, even when the piece represents an ally.
Players cannot reveal a concealed enemy by guessing its token identifier.
Use Fit to restore a useful camera view after zooming into a creature.

creatures.name: Skeleton
creatures.tagline: The dead remember how to march
tips: A skeleton is an animated undead creature rather than a living humanoid.
Its exposed bones give the encounter a different character from a shambling zombie.
Clattering steps and abandoned equipment can introduce an undead patrol.
An ancient command may explain why a skeleton still guards an empty room.
This Skeleton showcase loops with sound. Pause, replay, mute or adjust its volume using the controls below.
Holy material uses hard glints and light facets rather than yellow flame.
A Holy nova is an instant effect centered on the cursor's release position.
Fog can conceal only part of a room while leaving the entrance visible.
Darkvision shows unlit map detail in grayscale and creates no light source.
Save a reusable visual effect as a named table preset.

creatures.name: Zombie
creatures.tagline: One more step through the dark
tips: A zombie is a reanimated corpse whose persistence can surprise an attacker.
Its shambling appearance makes a useful contrast with quicker undead.
A familiar uniform or possession can tell the story of who the creature once was.
A slow threat can still become urgent when the party is trapped.
The model has colored decaying skin, wounds and torn clothing.
Death FX form moving wisps and dark vapor instead of purple fire.
Blood FX produce fluid sheets, falling droplets and suspended mist.
Apply appearance in Tokens to update the selected piece's name and size together.
The DM decides whether a creature is visible; owning another token does not bypass fog.
Right-drag the loading model vertically to bring a detail into a better viewing position.

creatures.name: Wraith
tips: A wraith is an incorporeal undead threat, unlike a creature built from bone or flesh.
Its presence can make darkness feel like an active part of the encounter.
A spectral foe invites descriptions of cold, silence and distorted light.
The history of a haunting can offer another path besides a fight.
This floating sculpture has a colored hood, spectral hands and trailing cloth.
Smoke material rolls into layered billows with changing silhouettes.
Reduce motion on your device when a calmer effect display is more comfortable.
Moonlight strength and sunlight strength can be adjusted independently.
A blackout is a deliberate DM action and does not erase the player's sheet.
A remembered player identity restores only the grants that exist in the saved campaign.

creatures.name: Giant Spider
tips: A giant spider's climbing and webs let it threaten more than the floor.
Threads across a doorway can be an early warning of a webbed lair.
An ambush becomes clearer when players can identify cover and escape routes.
Describe ceiling height when a creature can attack from above.
The colored model has eight jointed legs, several eyes and paired fangs.
Use the foreground layer for objects that sit visually above tokens.
Foreground scenery fades when it overlaps a token so the piece stays readable.
A persistent measuring shape can show a hazardous webbed area.
Water FX create splash droplets and ripples, with motion distinct from sticky Slime.
Turn up grid opacity when roots, webs or stones make square boundaries hard to see.

creatures.name: Basilisk
creatures.tagline: Do not meet its golden eyes
tips: The basilisk is an eight-legged reptilian monstrosity associated with petrification.
A field of strangely lifelike statues can be a warning before the creature is seen.
A gaze threat makes the decision to look away meaningful.
Give players clear descriptions of what their characters can and cannot see.
Rotate the sculpture to count its legs and examine the ridge of spines.
Frost FX form sharp shards and branching crystal shapes instead of blue flames.
Instant effects need no source: aim the cursor and release the left mouse button.
A visual flash is a cue for the table, not automatic application of a condition.
The compass sets board north; it does not rotate the map's artwork or grid.
Use the model viewer's reset control to return to its original angle and height.

creatures.name: Rust Monster
tips: A rust monster is known for its appetite for metal and its sensitive antennae.
The threat to equipment can matter more than raw damage.
Corroded tools and missing metal fittings can foreshadow its presence.
An encounter goal might be recovering supplies rather than defeating every creature.
This model includes an armored back, long antennae and a fan-shaped tail.
Create a creature token first, then explicitly choose its controller if a player needs it.
Setting Controlled by to DM only removes the player's movement access.
The grid's color, opacity and thickness are saved separately for each scene.
Saved FX presets retain their material as well as their tint.
Keep your local player identity when returning to a campaign so your grants can be restored.

creatures.name: Carrion Crawler
tips: A carrion crawler is a scavenging monstrosity with a mass of dangerous tentacles.
Its many legs and feelers suit cramped, filthy underground passages.
A trail through abandoned refuse can warn explorers that something feeds nearby.
An encounter can turn on helping an ally escape a creature's reach.
Rotate the segmented colored model to inspect its tentacles and many feet.
Use a circle template to discuss reach or the extent of a hazard.
The ruler can add waypoints while preserving one continuous measurement.
An FX pool stays under the release point even if you began the click elsewhere.
Only the DM can change a token's layer, concealment or control assignment.
A player who reconnects proves their saved identity rather than relying on a display name.

creatures.name: Purple Worm
tips: A purple worm is an enormous burrowing monstrosity with a terrible maw.
Its size can turn a cave system into the creature's own passageway.
Rumbling stone and sudden tremors can build tension before the first sighting.
A chase, collapsing tunnel or escape route can give a giant-monster encounter variety.
Inspect the colored sculpture's segmented plates, ringed mouth and tail stinger.
Zoom out in the model viewer to take in a creature with a broad silhouette.
Scale FX to fit a dramatic moment while keeping the grid readable.
Non-cast explosions do not draw a trajectory across the board.
The DM can add a sample scene without replacing the campaign's existing maps.
Bring the party to another scene only when the gallery's party option is selected.

creatures.name: Gibbering Mouther
creatures.tagline: Too many voices, too many eyes
tips: A gibbering mouther is an amorphous aberration covered in eyes and mouths.
Its unsettling sounds make the encounter more than a visual threat.
Distorted ground and confused movement can help describe an alien presence.
A creature's strange behavior can be a clue that ordinary tactics may fail.
This sculpture has individually modeled eyes, mouths and fleshy tendrils.
Charm FX flutter as hearts and petals; Magic FX trace moving arcane patterns.
Materials remain distinct even when you choose the same custom color for both.
The live FX preview is local until you deliberately place the effect on the board.
Your display name can change without giving up the identity that holds your token grants.
The creature codex offers twenty models and ten tailored tips for each, even after loading finishes.
